topics.title: Newton's Laws of Motion and Force Systems

subtopics.title: Inertia, Inertial Reference Frames, and the First Law
subtopics.description: Galileo's principle of inertia; operational definition of inertial frames; zero net force implies constant velocity.

subtopics.title: Linear Momentum, Impulse, and the Second Law
subtopics.description: Differential relation F_net = dp/dt = m dv/dt = m a for constant mass; vector decomposition; impulse J = int F dt = delta p.

subtopics.title: Action-Reaction Pairs and the Third Law
subtopics.description: Mutual interaction forces F_AB = -F_BA; distinct points of application; impossibility of self-canceling internal pairs.

subtopics.title: Free-Body Diagrams and Component Equations
subtopics.description: Systematic isolation of bodies; classification of contact forces (normal, tension, spring) and field forces (weight mg); orthogonal coordinate projection.

subtopics.title: String and Pulley Kinematic Constraints
subtopics.description: Ideal massless inextensible strings; massless frictionless pulleys; length preservation sum(l_i) = const; virtual work constraint sum(T_i . a_i) = 0.

subtopics.title: Wedge and Incline Surface Constraints
subtopics.description: Rigid boundary non-penetration condition; perpendicular velocity and acceleration equality at movable contact interfaces.

subtopics.title: Non-Inertial Reference Frames and Pseudo-Forces
subtopics.description: Linearly accelerating observers; inertial force F_pseudo = -m a_0; apparent weight in accelerating elevators; equilibrium analysis in accelerating frames.

subtopics.title: Microscopic Origin and Nature of Friction
subtopics.description: Intermolecular adhesion at microscopic asperities; cold-welding; normal force proportionality; independence of macroscopic contact area.

subtopics.title: Static Friction and Limiting Value
subtopics.description: Self-adjusting tangential force 0 <= f_s <= f_s,max = mu_s N; onset of relative motion.

subtopics.title: Kinetic (Sliding) Friction
subtopics.description: Constant dynamic resisting force f_k = mu_k N opposing relative sliding velocity; mu_k <= mu_s.

subtopics.title: Stacked Multi-Body Systems (Two-Block Problems)
subtopics.description: Friction between moving bodies; threshold driving force for relative slip; transition from unified acceleration to independent sliding accelerations.

subtopics.title: Friction and Limiting Equilibrium on Curved Surfaces
subtopics.description: Equilibrium of particle on rough hemispherical or cylinder bowl; local tangent and normal resolution; angle bounds.

subtopics.title: Angle of Repose and Angle of Friction
subtopics.description: Critical incline angle theta_R = arctan(mu_s) for sliding onset; resultant contact reaction force angle lambda = arctan(mu).

subtopics.title: Centripetal Force and Radial Dynamics
subtopics.description: Net inward radial force F_r = m v^2 / R = m omega^2 R sustaining curved trajectory; physical identification of inward agent.

subtopics.title: Banking of Roads and Tracks
subtopics.description: Optimum design speed v_0 = sqrt(R g tan(theta)) without lateral friction; safe speed envelopes [v_min, v_max] under static friction mu_s.

subtopics.title: Centrifugal Force in Rotating Frames
subtopics.description: Outward pseudo-force m omega^2 r in uniformly rotating coordinate frame; centrifugal potential and static equilibrium in rotating tubes.

subtopics.title: The Conical Pendulum
subtopics.description: String tension horizontal component T sin(theta) supplying centripetal acceleration; vertical equilibrium T cos(theta) = mg; revolution period T = 2 pi sqrt(L cos(theta) / g).

explicit_exclusions.topic: Work-Energy Theorem and Conservative Potential Energy
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Reserved strictly for Chapter 4: Work, Energy and Power.
Non-uniform circular motion requiring conservation of mechanical energy belongs to Chapter 4: Work, Energy and Power.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Multi-Particle Collisions and Center of Mass Momentum
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Internal impulse, center of mass kinematics, and restitution coefficients belong to Chapter 5: Center of Mass and Linear Momentum.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Rotational Torque and Moment of Inertia
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Rigid body rotational dynamics tau = I alpha and angular momentum belong to Chapter 6: Rotational Motion.
Inverse square gravitational law and Keplerian orbits belong to Chapter 7: Gravitation.

primary_sources.title: Concepts of Physics Vol 1 by H.C. Verma
primary_sources.coverage: Chapter 4: The Forces (pp. 66-73), Chapter 5: Newton's Laws of Motion (pp. 74-94), Chapter 6: Friction (pp. 95-110), Chapter 7: Circular Motion (pp. 111-125)
primary_sources.role: Rigorous definition of inertial frames, free-body diagram isolation, friction mechanisms, pulley-incline systems, worked examples, exercise problems

primary_sources.title: Fundamentals of Physics (Halliday, Resnick & Walker)
primary_sources.coverage: Chapter 5: Force and Motion—I (pp. 115-144) & Chapter 6: Force and Motion—II (pp. 145-172)
primary_sources.role: Calculus-based dynamics, static/kinetic friction transitions, drag forces, banking of curves, uniform circular dynamics

primary_sources.title: University Physics with Modern Physics (Young & Freedman)
primary_sources.coverage: Chapter 4: Newton's Laws of Motion (pp. 131-168) & Chapter 5: Applying Newton's Laws (pp. 169-214)
primary_sources.role: Systematic free-body methodology, multi-body coupled constraints, banking angle derivations, conical pendulum dynamics

primary_sources.title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Vol. 1
primary_sources.coverage: Lecture 9: Newton's Laws of Dynamics & Lecture 12: Characteristics of Force
primary_sources.role: Fundamental physical intuition on force as interaction, operational limits of classical mechanics, non-inertial pseudo-forces

primary_sources.title: Problems in General Physics by I.E. Irodov
primary_sources.coverage: Part 1, Section 1.2: The Fundamental Equation of Dynamics (pp. 17-26, Problems 1.59 to 1.120)
primary_sources.role: Advanced constraint problems, movable wedges, two-block threshold friction, circular dynamics under friction
